problem: Existing VLN benchmarks assume the human knows the environment and gives explicit step-by-step instructions (Human Guidance VLN). In real scenarios humans are unfamiliar with the environment and give only destination-related information, so the agent must plan the path itself.
motivation: Real-world assistant robots must navigate for users who can only state the destination. Mainstream VLN methods fail to process such destination-only instructions, so a new task, dataset and a paradigm shift are needed.
key_idea: Introduce the Human Assistant VLN (HA-VLN) task with the R2RA dataset (restructured from R2R), and HAVEN, an LLM with an embedded memory system that plugs into existing VLN methods to handle destination-only instructions.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that pairing an LLM with an embedded memory lets existing VLN agents cope with destination-only instructions without extra information, and that HAVEN can be plugged into any VLN method as an end-to-end module.
method: HA-VLN task: humans supply only destination-related information and the agent must plan the path itself.
R2RA dataset: the classic R2R dataset restructured into destination-oriented instructions for HA-VLN.
HAVEN: an evolution network that integrates an LLM with an embedded memory system.
Plug-in design: an end-to-end module that can be integrated into any VLN method, with no additional information required.

setting.backbone: LLM (unspecified) with memory system, integrated into existing VLN methods
setting.training_data: R2RA (restructured R2R); details not given in the abstract
setting.privileged: none stated (claims no additional information required)

results: The abstract states that algorithms incorporating HAVEN achieve higher success rates, shorter paths and lower navigation error on HA-VLN. No numbers or baselines are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details and numbers are unverified.
